decision.summary: Filtered automatic Harmony instrumentation is feasible for an explicit, bounded set of managed non-open-generic methods, with exact call accounting and inclusive timing. It is not suitable for hard-reload/collectible contexts in this version and has high per-call overhead.

environment.note: Single-process Stopwatch micro-measurement; indicative, not BenchmarkDotNet-grade.

limitations.evidence: A collectible AssemblyLoadContext remained alive after explicit owner UnpatchAll, counter-key removal, context.Unload, 20 forced GC/finalizer cycles, and 25 ms between cycles.
limitations.implication: Do not use this Lib.Harmony 2.3.6 design where collectible assembly unload or Godot hard reload is required. Process/domain restart is the reliable cleanup boundary.

limitations.evidence: Harmony patching an open generic definition threw NotSupportedException from MonoMod MMReflectionImporter.ImportGenericParameter on .NET 8.
limitations.implication: Preview classifies open generics as skipped; explicit closed instantiation support would require a separate design.

limitations.evidence: AggressiveInlining methods can be patched and observed in this test, but callers compiled before patching or tiered-JIT decisions can bypass detours.
limitations.implication: Inlining coverage cannot be guaranteed for arbitrary production methods.

limitations.evidence: Measured disabled overhead 166.336 ns/call and enabled overhead 189.616 ns/call in the recorded run.
limitations.implication: Keep selection narrow and avoid hot trivial methods.
